function: Learned refinement of coarse least-squares MIMO channel estimates under few pilots using RSS-map side information, plus multi-step prediction of future channel snapshots (pp. 1, 4, 8-9).
system: Downlink, BS 24x24 URA, vehicular user 2x2 URA, 16 taps; urban ray tracing at 15 GHz (400 MHz) and 8 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3, 10, 12).
method: Physics-informed ResUNet with transformer layers and cross-attention to an RSS-map encoder; supervised NMSE plus power-conservation loss; fine-tuning transfer to new frequency or site (pp. 6-8, 14).
data_channel: Own Wireless InSite ray-tracing datasets: Boston map (9877 samples, 15 and 8 GHz) and urban canyon; 80/10/10 split; RSS maps from ray tracing (pp. 9-10, 12).
test_conditions: Trained on Boston 15 GHz, tested on held-out 10%; zero-shot and fine-tuned transfer to 8 GHz and to urban canyon; other array sizes retrained (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Classical LS variants, OMP, SOMP, Subspace Pursuit; learned CNN estimator inspired by [9] and diffusion-model estimator [12] (p. 13).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus SNR, pilots, transmit antennas, prediction horizon and speed; FLOPs, latency, parameters (pp. 11, 13-16).
complexity: Big-O of PINN (eq. 28); 70.85 GFLOPs, 11.12 ms latency, 3.5e8 parameters versus diffusion model 130.15 GFLOPs, 50.30 ms, 5.5e4 parameters (pp. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 9: "we used Wireless InSite [27] for generating communication channels" Not met: the authors build their own ray-tracing datasets (Boston and urban canyon scenes); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "The model was initially trained on the 15 GHz dataset and then fine-tuned on 8 GHz data" Table 11 also gives zero-shot results from Boston 15 GHz to 8 GHz and to the urban canyon.
q3_support: p. 13: "We also implement a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based channel estimation structure inspired by [9]" Also a diffusion model [12]; classical OMP, SOMP and Subspace Pursuit are compared on NMSE in Fig. 9.
q4_support: p. 11: "our PINN requires significantly fewer FLOPs and achieves much lower inference latency" Table 7 gives 70.85 GFLOPs, 11.12 ms and 3.5e8 parameters; Big-O in eq. 28 (p. 10).
q5_support: p. 9: "The code and dataset used to obtain the experimental results presented in this section are provided in [41]." Ref. [41] is the GitHub link (p. 17).
notes: Area 2: channel estimation (with a temporal prediction extension). q1=0 is a judgement call: own Wireless InSite ray-tracing datasets built on Remcom example scenes (p. 9) and released with the paper, but not DeepMIMO, 3GPP or measured data; the reviewer may count them as public ray-tracing data. q2=1: zero-shot and fine-tuned transfer across frequency and site (Table 11, p. 14). q3=1: learned CNN [9] and diffusion [12] plus classical OMP, SOMP, Subspace Pursuit and LS, all on NMSE (p. 13). q4=1: Big-O and measured FLOPs, latency, parameters (pp. 10-11). q5=1: code and data on GitHub (p. 9). Title and DOI on p. 1 match.
